newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks firm ahead of Greenspan testimony.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks firm ahead of Greenspan testimony.

text.p: Wall Street shares were higher at midday Tuesday, as traders and investors awaited Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on the economy with an optimism tinged slightly with caution.
A firmer bond market, solid earnings reports and bargain-hunting also bolstered share prices, analysts said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up about 56 points, or 0.71 percent, at 7963, off its session highs.
The Nasdaq composite, whose technology stocks recently suffered profit-taking, rose 10 points to 1546.
The long bond lent support to equities markets, rising 11/32 to yield 6.51 percent.
Markets were also helped by a stronger dollar, which encouraged foreign investors to buy U.S. assets, analysts said. The dollar was trading at 1.8170/75 marks.

"The market seems to believe Greenspan will not say anything extreme," Barbara Marcin, vice president of Citibank Global Asset Management, said. "We worried about it a little bit yesterday, but the bond market has come back to where it was."
The Fed chief will deliver his mandatory, semiannual testimony on the economy and monetary policy to Congress at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT. He will also address Congress on Wednesday.

Markets would pay close attention for any remarks about inflation or stock valuations, analysts said. But some said there was little Greenspan could say that would derail the rosy scenario for the U.S. economy.

"The economy is still performing extremely well....The inflation outlook is benign, and it is hard to conceive of a change in interest rates to the upside," Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp, said.
"It looks like there is nothing out there to derail that, but the market would like to get past Greenspan," Stein said.
Share prices were also gaining because investors had booked some profits recently, analysts said.

"Investors are using any excuse to be buyers," Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross, said. "A modest recovery in bonds and, essentially, a three-day decline in stocks, is enough to bring in buyers."
Solid second-quarter earnings helped push the broader stock market higher, too, analyst said.
Dow component Philip Morris Cos Inc posted second-quarter earnings of $0.76 per share versus $0.66 per share in last year's second quarter and in line with the First Call consensus earnings estimate.
Shares of the cigarette maker were up 1-12/16 to 42-5/16.
Walt Disney Co stock rose 1-10/16 to 76-13/16, after reporting third-quarter earnings of $0.69 per share compared to a pro forma $0.58 per share a year ago.
But International Business Machines Corp, whose stock had been strong ahead of its quarterly earning, fell 1-14/16 to 101-13/16 after the report, released late Monday.

The sprawling technology company posted second-quarter earnings of $1.46 per share compared with $1.26 per share post-split in last year's second quarter, and above Wall Street estimates of $1.42 per share.
Other technology stocks resumed their upward rise after several days of profit-taking.
Dell Computer Corp stock rose 5-1/8 to 157-3/4 and Microsoft Corp gained 3-1/32 to 138-31/32.
Tupperware Corp fell 2-7/8 to 34-5/8 after reporting second-quarter earnings fell to $0.61 per share from $0.77 in the year-ago quarter.
((Wall Street desk 212-859-1730))
